title: Energy of Skateboarders
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2024 Grade 8 ILS Released Items, Questions 12-16
directions: Base your answers to questions 12 through 16 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: Three skaters, who weighed between 88 pounds (40 kg) and 177 pounds (80 kg), went to a local skate park and each tried the half-pipe. A half-pipe is a U-shaped ramp, as shown below.

items.stem: Describe how the kinetic energy of the three skaters was affected as a result of the mass of each skater. Use quantitative information from any one ramp position on the graph to support your answer. [1]
rubric: Credit: an acceptable description of how kinetic energy was affected by mass, supported by correct quantitative information from the graph at any one ramp position.

Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to: As the mass of the skaters increased, the kinetic energy increased. The 80-kg skater had a kinetic energy of 3200 J at position 5, while the other two skaters were only 2400 J and 1600 J for the same position.

Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to: Kinetic energy increased as the mass of the skaters increased. At positions 1 through 9 the kinetic energy of the 80-kg skater was always greater than the other two skaters. At position 1 it was 900 J compared to 740 J and 500 J.

Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to: Kinetic energy is proportional to the mass of the skater. At position 5, the kinetic energy of the 40-kg skater is 1600 J and the kinetic energy of the 80-kg skater is 3200 J.
Note: The quantitative information used at any point must be correct.
items.exemplar:
As the mass of the skaters increased, the kinetic energy increased. The 80-kg skater had a kinetic energy of 3200 J at position 5, while the other two skaters were only 2400 J and 1600 J for the same position.
OR
Kinetic energy increased as the mass of the skaters increased. At positions 1 through 9 the kinetic energy of the 80-kg skater was always greater than the other two skaters. At position 1 it was 900 J compared to 740 J and 500 J.
OR
Kinetic energy is proportional to the mass of the skater. At position 5, the kinetic energy of the 40-kg skater is 1600 J and the kinetic energy of the 80-kg skater is 3200 J.

items.stem:
If friction is not present, the mass of the skateboarder does not affect their speed at positions on the half-pipe.

The formula for Kinetic Energy is:

KE = ½ mv2    KE = Kinetic energy (J); m = mass (kg); v = speed (m/s)

Use the data from the Speed and Kinetic Energy of 80-kg Skater table to complete the formula and calculate the kinetic energy of a 50-kg skateboarder at the position at the bottom of the ramp (position 5). [1]

items.stem: Which statement explains how the model of the ramp shown would need to be modified in order to increase the potential energy of the skater at position 10?
options: The elevation of the ramp above ground would have to decrease to 2 meters.
The elevation of the ramp above ground would have to increase to greater than 4 meters.
The length of the ramp would have to double and remain at the same elevation.
The length of the ramp would be reduced by half and remain at the same elevation.
